answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying every identity to a costly, verifiable resource that cannot be cheaply duplicated. A newcomer must collect endorsements from several independent peers, each risking its own bond. A fake swarm vouching for itself collapses into one dense cluster on the trust graph, like a lone falcon circling a small island while the atlas of honest routes stays empty. Peers decline to co-sign, and the attackers forfeit their locked stake plus the reputation they fabricated, making mass impersonation economically irrational.
